sections.title: The question we can always answer
sections.body:
> At any moment we can answer: why can't this team send, who decided that, and what would change it?

Today a reviewer rebuilds that answer from a disabled flag, a pile of suspicious-activity rows and thousands of notice cards. The answer should come from one place and reach three audiences in their own words.

- **The sender** sees which domain is paused, the reason in plain words, and what happens next. The API returns the same reason.
- **Support** reads the reason the sender saw, plus the decider and the evidence.
- **The reviewer** sees what is keeping the domain disabled, lifts exactly that, and says whether the check was wrong or the sender fixed it.

sections.title: 1 · A restriction is a claim with a reason and a decider
sections.body:
```
every Restriction has
  category
  ∧ (ruleId ∨ decider = person)
  ∧ decider ∈ { person, automation@version }
```

**Breaks when** a domain is disabled and nobody can say which check or person did it.

**Caught by** NOT NULL and CHECK constraints on the table, and every disable call site going through one model function that takes the claim.

sections.title: 2 · The remedy matches the finding
sections.body:
```
lift(restriction) and allow(selector) act at the grain
the finding was made: an email, a word, a rule, a team
```

**Breaks when** approving one flagged email re-enables a domain that was disabled for a bounce spike.

That break is live today. It's the first fix on the path, and it needs no new tables.

sections.title: 3 · Detectors are provisional, people are binding
sections.body:
**Lift** means "this reason no longer blocks the domain". It's today's Re-enable button, but aimed at one reason instead of the whole domain. Nothing is deleted. The restriction row gets three fields filled once: who lifted it, the verdict, and a note.

```
lift      needs  person ∧ verdict ∈ { wrong, fixed } ∧ note
allowance needs  person ∧ until
```

**Breaks when** a reviewer re-enables with no record of whether the detector misfired. Without the verdict we can't measure a detector's false-positive rate or tune it.

sections.title: 4 · Write once, compute everything else
sections.body:
```
sendingDomain.disabled  ⇔  ∃ restriction in effect on (domain ∨ team)
only restrict() and lift() change it
```

**Breaks when** any code path flips `disabled` directly, or edits a past row.

The timeline, the "keeping it disabled" panel, the sender's banner and the API reason are all reads over the same rows.

sections.title: Three nouns, nothing else
sections.body:
A new noun needs a real case these three can't express.

| Noun        | Holds                                                        | Changes by                         |
|-------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| Restriction | team, domain (empty = team), category, ruleId, findingKey,   | written once; lifted once with     |
|             | decider                                                      | verdict + note                     |
| Allowance   | one selector: finding (word:acme) | rule | category | all;   | granted, expires, or revoked       |
|             | until, granted by, note                                      |                                    |
| Registry    | categories + rules with sender-facing copy                   | a code change                      |

sections.title: Reviewer · notice chart (built)
sections.body:
**Today** one card per 15-minute reading. A week is ~670 cards per type, mostly Info, and they push the content findings off the page.

```
┌ Spam · Info        0.09% · Oct 28 14:07 ┐
┌ Bounce · Info      0.61% · Oct 28 14:22 ┐
┌ Spam · Info        0.11% · Oct 28 14:37 ┐
┌ ApplePrivateRelay · Info  0.02% · 14:52 ┐
┌ Spam · Error       0.41% · Oct 28 15:07 ┐   ← the one that matters
┌ Bounce · Info      0.58% · Oct 28 15:22 ┐
  … 2,000 more
```

**After** one chart per type, labelled with what the rate is out of. A type that reached Error turns red.

```
╔ Spam complaints  per non-Gmail delivery  [Error] ═══ peak 0.41% · 6 h at Error ╗
║                                          ●●                                     ║
║                                        ●●  ●●                                   ║
║ ─────────────────────────────────────╱──────╲────────────────────────────────── ║
╚═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ ▸ Hourly ══╝
┌ Hard bounces  per delivery ─────────────────────── peak 1.80% · 4 h at Warning ┐
│              ○○                                                                 │
│ ────────────╱──╲─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── ▸ Hourly ─┘
```

Five stacked PRs, gates-green, yours to push. It's a read over rows we already write, so it doesn't wait on the new tables.

sections.title: Reviewer · what keeps this domain disabled
sections.body:
```
admin › domain review › mail.acme-example.com
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ ■ Disabled — 2 restrictions in effect. Lifting both re-enables.  │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Possible phishing in "Reset your password"     [Lift…] [Email]   │
│ content.phishing · phishing_classifier · automation@v14 · Oct 28 │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Complaint rate 0.41% over 24h                  [Lift…] [Chart]   │
│ behavior.complaint_rate · health_complaint_limit · automation    │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ ░ Banned word "bitcoin" in "Weekly digest"            lifted     │
```

Lifting the phishing restriction leaves the complaint-rate one in place, so the domain stays disabled. That's kernel 2.

sections.title: Reviewer · lift dialog and timeline
sections.body:
```
Lift: Possible phishing in "Reset your password"

  (●) The check was wrong         ( ) The sender fixed it
      Email is legitimate.            Finding was right;
      Counts against the detector.    the content changed.

  Note (required)
  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ Password reset for their own app, links to their site. │
  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                                          [Cancel] [Lift]
```

The timeline is computed from the rows, never written separately:

```
Oct 27 09:12  Restricted  banned word "bitcoin"   automation@banned-words
Oct 27 11:40  Lifted      wrong · Dana R. · allowance until Jan 27
Oct 28 14:07  Restricted  possible phishing       automation@v14
Oct 28 15:52  Restricted  complaint rate 0.41%    automation@health
```

sections.title: Sender · in-app banner and API
sections.body:
```
app › campaigns
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ ⚠ Sending from mail.acme-example.com is paused              │
│   One of your emails, "Reset your password", looked like    │
│   phishing to our automated checks. We're reviewing it and  │
│   will email you by the end of the next business day.       │
│   Other domains on your team can still send.                │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

```
POST /api/v1/transactional  → 403
{
  "success": false,
  "message": "Sending from mail.acme-example.com is paused.",
  "reason": {
    "category": "content.phishing",
    "summary": "An email looked like phishing to our automated checks.",
    "next": "under_review"
  }
}
```

The banner, the API and support all use the same registry copy. All copy here is a draft.

sections.title: Admin · domain review on the preview
Branch · disable markers in the viewer
Improve what we have
sections.body:
Each step is its own PR off main, and none needs new tables.

1. **Chart the account limit notices**: built, 5 PRs gates-green. *reviewer signal*
2. **Approving a flagged email re-enables only when nothing else holds the domain**: next; the live bug. *kernel 2*
   - Approve returns what's still blocking, and the toast says "Approved. mail.acme stays disabled: complaint rate hit Error Oct 28 15:52."
   - The review page lists "Still keeping this domain disabled", computed from signals we already store: unreviewed flagged emails, health readings at Error since the disable, and team flags.
   - On main today a disable doesn't record its cause (DisableDomainEvent only has `decision`), so this list is inferred. That gap is what the Restriction table closes.
3. **The phishing check keeps its reason**: next. isSafe returns a tag that today's code throws away. *kernel 1*
4. **Workflow preflight disables the failing email's domain**: candidate, needs a check. Today it disables the team's first sending domain. *kernel 2*
5. **Collapse notice runs in the team feed**: candidate. It's the same deluge, on the team page. *reviewer signal*

sections.title: Then add the new thing
sections.body:
A spine in ladder order, sliced from the local spike (41 passing tests).

1. **Add the Restriction and Allowance tables and the registry**: CHECKs enforce "exactly one selector" and "lift fields written together". *kernels 1 · 3*
2. **Every disable writes a restriction**: all ten call sites pass a claim, and `disabled` is set only by restrict() and lift(). *kernel 4*
3. **Lift with a verdict, allow with an expiry**: an admin block picker, the lift dialog, and detectors that check allowances. *kernels 2 · 3*
4. **Show what keeps the domain disabled**: the reviewer mockup. *kernel 4*
5. **Give the sender and the API the reason**: the sender mockup. *kernel 4*

sections.title: Still to decide
sections.body:
- Sender-facing copy per category, and who owns it: support or product.
- Is "hold a publish" (LOO-6309) a restriction on one email, or its own thing? Kernel 2 points to a restriction with an email finding.
- The complaint rate excludes only exact `@gmail.com`. Workspace and googlemail recipients still count. Fix the denominator or label it as it is.
